$comment: Authoritative catalog of JuLC compiler diagnostics. Each entry has a stable JULC#### code, a generated Java constant, an emitted-message template, a one-line root cause, a canonical fix snippet, and optionally example bad/good code. Consumed by: (1) generated DiagnosticCodes.java, (2) the MCP julc_explain_diagnostic tool, (3) docs/AI catalog resources, (4) future full compiler diagnostic coverage tests.

categories.SYNTAX: Java syntax forms not supported in the on-chain subset
categories.STDLIB: Stdlib method usage errors (wrong arity, missing args)
categories.BACKEND: Language-neutral backend descriptors and producer PIR verification
categories.FRONTEND: The javac frontend and its closed compilation environment (ADR-068)

diagnostics.title: Method must have a body
diagnostics.template: Method must have a body: {0}
diagnostics.summary: A method with no body, such as an abstract or interface method, was found where the compiler lowers a method. Emitted by the javac frontend (ADR-068 I2a); the reference frontend reports it uncoded.
diagnostics.fix: Provide a body for every method in your validator class.

diagnostics.title: Variable must be initialized
diagnostics.template: Variable must be initialized: {0}
diagnostics.summary: A local variable was declared without an initializer. UPLC has no notion of uninitialized state. Emitted by the javac frontend (ADR-068 I2a); the reference frontend reports it uncoded.
diagnostics.fix: Initialize at declaration, e.g. `var x = BigInteger.ZERO;`. Re-bind via a new `var` if you need a different value later (UPLC is single-assignment).

example.bad:
var x;
x = 5;
example.good: var x = BigInteger.valueOf(5);

diagnostics.title: return inside a while loop
diagnostics.template: 'return' is not supported inside while loop body
diagnostics.summary: A `while` loop body cannot `return` from the enclosing method. A `while` loop is compiled to a recursive function whose result is the variables the loop updates, so it has no way to leave the method early. The diagnostic points at the first such `return`.
diagnostics.fix: Exit the loop with break, or keep the result in a variable declared before the loop, and return after the loop.

diagnostics.title: break statement outside of a loop
diagnostics.template: break is only supported inside for-each or while loops on-chain
diagnostics.summary: `break` was used outside of a `for-each` or `while` loop body, such as in a `switch` statement. Emitted by the javac frontend (ADR-068 I2a); the reference frontend reports it uncoded.
diagnostics.fix: Use for-each or while with an accumulator and break to exit early

diagnostics.title: Switch is not exhaustive on sealed interface
diagnostics.template: Switch on sealed interface {0} is not exhaustive. Missing cases: {1}
diagnostics.summary: A `switch` expression on a sealed interface is missing one or more permitted variants. Only unguarded case labels count: a label whose guard is not the constant `true` may not apply, so it does not cover its variant (JLS 14.11.1.1, ADR-067 D4).
diagnostics.fix: Add the missing case branches (an unguarded one per variant when the others are guarded) or include a `default ->` branch to handle all remaining variants.

diagnostics.title: Method does not return on all paths
diagnostics.template: Method ''{0}'' may not return a value on all execution paths
diagnostics.summary: A non-void method has at least one execution path that does not return a value. Emitted by the javac frontend (ADR-068 I2a); the reference frontend reports it uncoded.
diagnostics.fix: Ensure all code paths end with a 'return' statement.

diagnostics.title: Switch expression requires a sealed interface type
diagnostics.template: switch expression requires a sealed interface type, got: {0}
diagnostics.summary: `switch` was used on a type that is not a sealed interface, or on a sealed interface that declares type parameters. Records (including `Tuple2`/`Tuple3`) cannot be switched on. JuLC drops type arguments, so it cannot decide which variants of a parameterized sealed interface apply or whether a switch over one is exhaustive (ADR-067 D4).
diagnostics.fix: Use field access (`pair.first()`, `pair.second()`) for records. Reserve `switch` for sealed interfaces with permitted record variants.

diagnostics.title: @Entrypoint method has wrong parameter count
diagnostics.template: {0} entrypoint must have {1} parameters{2}, found {3} in {4}.{5}(){6}
diagnostics.summary: The @Entrypoint method's parameter count doesn't match the validator kind. SpendingValidator entrypoints take 2 or 3 params (datum, redeemer, ctx); other validators take 2 (redeemer, ctx).
diagnostics.fix: Adjust the entrypoint signature to match the validator annotation. Spending: `(Datum, Redeemer, ScriptContext)`. Others: `(Redeemer, ScriptContext)`.

diagnostics.title: No @Entrypoint method found
diagnostics.template: No @Entrypoint method found in {0}
diagnostics.summary: The validator class has no method annotated `@Entrypoint`.
diagnostics.fix: Annotate exactly one `public static` method with `@Entrypoint`. The method must return `boolean` (or `void` for newer signature shapes).

diagnostics.title: No validator annotation found
diagnostics.template: No validator annotation found{0}
diagnostics.summary: The class has no validator annotation. Expected one of @SpendingValidator, @MintingValidator, @CertifyingValidator, @WithdrawValidator, @VotingValidator, @ProposingValidator (or @MultiValidator).
diagnostics.fix: Add the appropriate validator annotation at the class level.

diagnostics.title: Undefined variable
diagnostics.template: Undefined variable: {0}
diagnostics.summary: A name was read that the on-chain program has no binder for: a type or package read as a value, a class of a library the compilation cannot register, or a pattern variable outside the condition that binds it. Emitted by the javac frontend (ADR-068 I2a); the reference frontend reports it uncoded.
diagnostics.fix: Check spelling, or add an import if the name is a type. A pattern variable is bound only where its instanceof is the whole condition of an if.

diagnostics.title: Cannot resolve type
diagnostics.template: Cannot resolve type: {0}
diagnostics.summary: The compiler could not resolve a type reference. The class may not be on the classpath, may not be a registered ledger/stdlib type, or may not be a valid on-chain type.
diagnostics.fix: Ensure the type is imported and is one of: a record, sealed interface, ledger type, JulcList/JulcMap/Optional/Tuple, or primitive (BigInteger, byte[], boolean, String).
diagnostics.example: var a = JulcArray.of(BigInteger.ONE, new byte[]{1}); // elements of different types under var: declare JulcArray<T>

diagnostics.title: Banned @Param type
diagnostics.template: @Param type ''{0}'' is not allowed. @Param values are always raw Data at runtime; using a typed Data subtype causes the compiler to misinterpret the runtime representation.
diagnostics.summary: @Param fields cannot be raw `PlutusData` subtypes (`PlutusData.BytesData`, `PlutusData.MapData`, `PlutusData.ListData`, `PlutusData.IntData`) — these confuse the parameter wrapping pipeline.
diagnostics.fix: Use byte[], BigInteger, typed records, redeemers, or @Param PlutusData only for opaque data.

diagnostics.title: Arrays are not supported (except byte[])
diagnostics.template: arrays are not supported on-chain
diagnostics.summary: Java arrays other than a `byte[]` literal of integer literals are not supported on-chain. Emitted by the javac frontend (ADR-068 I2a); the reference frontend reports it uncoded.
diagnostics.fix: Use List<T> instead of arrays, or byte[] with literal initializers

diagnostics.title: try/catch is not supported on-chain
diagnostics.template: try/catch is not supported on-chain
diagnostics.summary: UPLC has no exception model — only `error` (immediate script failure).
diagnostics.fix: Use if/else checks instead of exception handling

diagnostics.title: throw is not supported on-chain
diagnostics.template: throw is not supported on-chain
diagnostics.summary: There is no exception machinery in UPLC.
diagnostics.fix: Return false from the validator to reject a transaction

diagnostics.title: null is not supported on-chain
diagnostics.template: null is not supported on-chain
diagnostics.summary: There is no `null` value in the on-chain type system.
diagnostics.fix: Use Optional<T> (Optional.of(x) / Optional.empty()) to represent absence of a value

diagnostics.title: C-style for loops are not supported
diagnostics.template: C-style for loops are not supported on-chain
diagnostics.summary: Only `for-each` (`for (var x : list)`) and `while` loops are supported on-chain.
diagnostics.fix: Use for-each over a list or while loops instead

diagnostics.title: do-while loops are not supported
diagnostics.template: do-while loops are not supported on-chain
diagnostics.summary: Do-while is not supported on-chain.
diagnostics.fix: Use while loops or for-each instead

diagnostics.title: Floating-point types are not supported
diagnostics.template: floating point types (float/double) are not supported on-chain
diagnostics.summary: `float` and `double` have no UPLC equivalent. Emitted by the javac frontend (ADR-068 I2a); the reference frontend reports it uncoded.
diagnostics.fix: Use BigInteger for integer arithmetic or Rational for fractions

diagnostics.title: Switch case field name shadows method parameter
diagnostics.template: Switch case binding name shadows a method parameter
diagnostics.summary: When a sealed-interface variant has a field with the same name as a method parameter, the field binding silently shadows the parameter inside the switch case body. The compiler may not always catch this — be vigilant.
diagnostics.fix: Always use distinct names. Example: rename `time` parameter to `point` when switching on `IntervalBoundType.Finite(time)`.

diagnostics.title: Lambda cannot be stored in a variable
diagnostics.template: Lambda cannot be stored in a variable
diagnostics.summary: Lambdas must be passed inline as arguments to higher-order functions. Storing a lambda in a `Function<X,Y>` variable and calling `.apply(...)` is not supported.
diagnostics.fix: Pass the lambda directly: `list.map(x -> ...)`, `list.filter(p -> ...)`. If you need to share lambda logic, extract it as a regular static method (not as a lambda).

diagnostics.title: Mutually recursive bindings with more than 2 participants not supported
diagnostics.template: Mutually recursive bindings with more than 2 participants not yet supported: {0}
diagnostics.summary: JuLC supports self-recursion and mutual recursion between exactly 2 helpers (via Bekic's theorem). Three or more mutually recursive functions are not supported.
diagnostics.fix: Refactor: combine the helpers into a single function with an accumulator, or break the recursion via an explicit dispatch on a sealed interface.

diagnostics.title: Unknown method on type
diagnostics.template: Unknown method: {0}
diagnostics.summary: A call names a method the on-chain program has no binder for, such as a generic template of a library class called from that class. Emitted by the javac frontend (ADR-068 I2a); the reference frontend reports it uncoded.
diagnostics.fix: Check the stdlib catalog at https://julc.dev/ai/catalog.json or the stdlib reference at https://julc.dev/stdlib/stdlib-guide/. Common: `JulcList<T>` has `head/tail/get/size/isEmpty/contains/prepend/reverse/concat/take/drop/map/filter/any/all/find`.

diagnostics.title: Stdlib method called with wrong number of arguments
diagnostics.template: Stdlib method called with wrong number of arguments: {0}
diagnostics.summary: A stdlib method was called with the wrong arity. Examples: `list.map()` requires a function argument, `list.contains()` requires an element argument, `map.insert()` requires (key, value).
diagnostics.fix: See the message itself — it includes a `Usage:` hint with the correct signature.

diagnostics.title: @NewType requires exactly one field
diagnostics.template: @NewType record {0} must have exactly one field
diagnostics.summary: @NewType is a single-field record wrapper around a primitive (byte[], BigInteger, String, boolean). Multi-field @NewType records are not allowed.
diagnostics.fix: Reduce to one field, or remove @NewType and use a plain record (which compiles to ConstrData).

diagnostics.title: Unsupported @NewType field type
diagnostics.template: Unsupported @NewType field type: {0}
diagnostics.summary: @NewType's underlying field must be a primitive: `byte[]`, `BigInteger`, `String`, or `boolean`.
diagnostics.fix: Change the underlying field to a supported primitive, or remove @NewType.

diagnostics.title: Failed to parse source
diagnostics.template: Failed to parse {0} source: {1}
diagnostics.summary: The Java source could not be parsed. Usually a syntax error in the source file.
diagnostics.fix: Check the file with a Java IDE or `javac` — the JuLC compiler relies on JavaParser to produce a clean AST.

diagnostics.title: Duplicate record / sealed interface type
diagnostics.template: Duplicate type declaration: {0}
diagnostics.summary: Two different declarations registered the same type name.
diagnostics.fix: Rename one of the types, or ensure they are not both on the compilation classpath.

diagnostics.title: Circular type dependency detected
diagnostics.template: Circular type dependency detected among: {0}
diagnostics.summary: Type registration found a cycle that cannot be resolved.
diagnostics.fix: Break the cycle by introducing a parameterized record or refactoring the involved types.

diagnostics.title: Unsupported compiler target
diagnostics.template: Compiler target {0} is not supported. Supported targets: {1}
diagnostics.summary: JuLC compilation is pinned to an explicit ledger language, protocol version, and UPLC version. Evaluator support for another profile does not imply compiler support.
diagnostics.fix: Select a listed compiler target. This release supports Plutus V3/PV11/UPLC 1.1.0 only; do not rely on fallback to another target.

diagnostics.title: Builtin unavailable for compiler target
diagnostics.template: Builtin {0} is not available for compiler target {1}
diagnostics.summary: A source lowering or low-level PIR route requested a builtin that is not in the canonical protocol feature profile selected for this compilation.
diagnostics.fix: Use an operation available in the selected target, or explicitly select a future compiler target after JuLC adds and verifies support for it.

diagnostics.title: Term or constant feature unavailable for compiler target
diagnostics.template: Compiler feature {0} is not available for compiler target {1}
diagnostics.summary: A lowering requires a UPLC term form or constant universe that the canonical protocol feature profile does not authorize.
diagnostics.fix: Use a portable lowering for the selected target, or add the future target through the reviewed compiler support process.

diagnostics.title: Generated UPLC version does not match compiler target
diagnostics.template: Generated UPLC version {0} does not match compiler target {1}, which requires {2}
diagnostics.summary: Program construction and the resolved compiler target disagreed. This is a compiler invariant violation, not a user source error.
diagnostics.fix: Report this as a JuLC compiler bug with the source, selected target, and verbose compiler log.

diagnostics.title: Compiler stage emitted a target-illegal feature
diagnostics.template: Compiler stage {0} emitted target-illegal feature {1} for {2}
diagnostics.summary: Final post-lowering validation found a builtin, term form, or constant universe that an earlier compiler stage should have rejected.
diagnostics.fix: Report this as a JuLC compiler bug. Include the named compiler stage/pass, selected target, and a minimal reproducer.

diagnostics.title: Compile and evaluation targets do not match
diagnostics.template: Compiled target {0} cannot be evaluated as {1}
diagnostics.summary: The evaluator must use the exact ledger language and protocol version retained by the compiler result.
diagnostics.fix: Evaluate with CompileResult.target().ledgerTarget(), or recompile for an explicitly supported compiler target.

diagnostics.title: Optimization cost profile is required
diagnostics.template: Optimization level {0} requires an explicit pinned optimization cost profile
diagnostics.summary: Legacy diagnostic retained for compatibility. No current compiler level consumes numeric cost parameters or requires a profile.
diagnostics.fix: Current compilation needs no cost profile. Configure cost parameters on the evaluator for budget measurements.

diagnostics.title: Optimization cost profile does not match compiler target
diagnostics.template: Optimization cost profile {0} targets {1}, but compiler target {2} evaluates as {3}
diagnostics.summary: A cost profile is valid only for the exact ledger language and protocol profile from which its parameters were pinned.
diagnostics.fix: Use a cost profile pinned for the selected compiler target, or select a compatible compiler target explicitly.

diagnostics.title: Unsupported optimization level
diagnostics.template: Optimization level {0} is not supported. Supported levels: {1}
diagnostics.summary: Optimizer selection uses an exact, versioned identifier and never falls back to a different rollout level.
diagnostics.fix: Select one of the listed optimization levels. Use baseline to preserve the pre-ADR-032 generated program.

diagnostics.title: Unsupported optimization cost profile
diagnostics.template: Optimization cost profile {0} is not supported. Supported profiles: {1}
diagnostics.summary: An explicitly supplied compatibility profile must identify a known immutable snapshot, even though current compiler rules do not consume it.
diagnostics.fix: Omit the unused compiler profile or select a listed ID, such as plutus-v3-pv11-costs-v1. Supply runtime cost parameters separately to the evaluator.

diagnostics.title: Native UPLC type mismatch
diagnostics.template: {0} received {1}, but requires {2}
diagnostics.summary: Opaque native UPLC values are not Data and cannot be passed through a differently typed compiler boundary.
diagnostics.fix: Use the matching typed native operation. Convert native Value explicitly with ValueData, or convert Data explicitly with UnValueData.

diagnostics.title: Native UPLC type at a Data argument boundary
diagnostics.template: Method parameter {0} has opaque type {1}, which cannot be decoded from a Plutus Data argument
diagnostics.summary: compileMethod and validator inputs are Data-encoded; a native evaluator value has no implicit Data representation.
diagnostics.fix: Accept PlutusData or a ledger type at the external boundary and call the explicit native conversion inside the method.

diagnostics.title: Unknown optimization rule in the disabled-rule set
diagnostics.template: Optimization rule {0} cannot be disabled. Rules that can be disabled: {1}
diagnostics.summary: Only the PIR-to-PIR sharing and promotion passes accept a per-rule switch; the identifier must match one of their rule ids exactly, so a typo never silently leaves the rule enabled.
diagnostics.fix: Use one of the listed rule identifiers exactly as reported in the optimization report, or lower the optimization level to disable a whole class of rules.

diagnostics.title: Unsupported backend contract revision
diagnostics.template: {0} targets backend contract revision {1}; this backend supports revisions {2}
diagnostics.summary: A neutral-backend descriptor or library provider declares a contract revision outside the range this compiler implements (ADR-059).
diagnostics.fix: Produce the descriptor for a supported revision reported by CompilerBackend.capabilities, or use a compiler release that implements the requested revision.

diagnostics.title: Required backend capability unavailable
diagnostics.template: {0} requires backend capability {1}, which is not available for {2}
diagnostics.summary: The descriptor declares a capability that this backend revision or compiler target does not provide, so compilation stops before materialization or lowering.
diagnostics.fix: Check CompilerBackend.capabilities for the selected target and remove the dependency on the missing capability, or select a target and compiler that provide it.

diagnostics.title: Producer target differs from the backend target
diagnostics.template: {0} was produced for target {1}, but the backend is configured for {2}
diagnostics.summary: Producer specialization and backend lowering must use the same ledger and UPLC profile; a mismatch would validate terms against the wrong builtin and feature set.
diagnostics.fix: Configure the producer and CompilerOptions with the same CompilerTarget.

diagnostics.title: Invalid neutral backend descriptor
diagnostics.template: Invalid descriptor {0}: {1}
diagnostics.summary: A neutral-backend descriptor is malformed: for example duplicate or reserved names, conflicting named type definitions, duplicate purposes or a handler signature that does not match its role.
diagnostics.fix: Correct the descriptor field named in the message; descriptors are validated before any provider materialization or lowering.

diagnostics.title: Invalid binding in producer PIR
diagnostics.template: Invalid PIR binding in {0}: {1}
diagnostics.summary: Producer PIR uses a reserved binder name, references a symbol that is not an import, definition or enclosing binder, or declares the same program-level name twice.
diagnostics.fix: Use producer-owned names that avoid the reserved forms (a leading '.' or '__', a leading '$julc$', or '#'), and reference imports only through the binding names returned by their provider.

diagnostics.title: Producer PIR types disagree
diagnostics.template: PIR type mismatch in {0}: {1}
diagnostics.summary: A producer term disagrees with a declared or synthesized type: a variable annotation differs from its binder, an argument does not match a parameter or builtin signature, a condition is not Bool, or branches disagree.
diagnostics.fix: Annotate the term with the type of the value it actually holds; convert between native and Data representations explicitly with the corresponding builtins.

diagnostics.title: Producer PIR structure unsupported by lowering
diagnostics.template: Unsupported PIR structure in {0}: {1}
diagnostics.summary: Producer PIR contains a form the lowering cannot compile correctly, such as a non-function recursive binding, a generator-local IntegerCase, a constructor or match that disagrees with its type layout, or an unresolved named type.
diagnostics.fix: Restructure the term as described; for example bind recursive values as lambdas and give a DataMatch exactly one branch per constructor in tag order.

diagnostics.title: Unsupported library request
diagnostics.template: Library request {0} is not supported: {1}
diagnostics.summary: A library provider cannot materialize the requested export, instantiation or type operation with a verified representation.
diagnostics.fix: Request only exports and operations the provider describes as supported; unsupported ones are listed with reasons by the provider.

diagnostics.title: Compound assignment operator is not supported
diagnostics.template: Compound assignment operator {0} is not supported on-chain
diagnostics.summary: Only +=, -=, *=, /= and %= on integers, and += on strings, are lowered. Bitwise, shift and boolean compound operators (&=, |=, ^=, <<=, >>=, >>>=) are rejected instead of being lowered with different semantics (ADR-060).
diagnostics.fix: Write the update explicitly. For booleans evaluate the check first so it always runs, as Java's &= does: boolean c = check(x); ok = ok && c;

diagnostics.title: More than one variable in a declaration
diagnostics.template: Declare one variable per statement: {0}
diagnostics.summary: A local declaration with several variables (BigInteger a = x, b = y;) is not lowered; only the first variable would be bound, so later references could resolve to an outer declaration of the same name (ADR-060).
diagnostics.fix: Split the declaration into one statement per variable.

example.bad: BigInteger a = BigInteger.ONE, b = BigInteger.TWO;
example.good:
BigInteger a = BigInteger.ONE;
BigInteger b = BigInteger.TWO;

diagnostics.title: Overloaded methods are not supported
diagnostics.template: Method {0} is declared more than once in {1}; on-chain methods are bound by name, so declarations sharing a name must compile to identical code
diagnostics.summary: Every call to an overloaded name would run one of its declarations. Declarations that lower to identical code and types are accepted; any other overload, or a helper that reuses an entrypoint's name, is rejected (ADR-060).
diagnostics.fix: Give each method a distinct name.

example.bad:
static boolean check(BigInteger a) { ... }
static boolean check(long a) { ... }
example.good:
static boolean checkAmount(BigInteger a) { ... }
static boolean checkIndex(long a) { ... }

diagnostics.title: Member access that cannot be resolved
diagnostics.template: Cannot resolve {0}: the receiver's type does not declare it as a record field, accessor or supported method
diagnostics.summary: x.name() and x.name resolve against the receiver's record, ledger or library type; record instance methods are not compiled. An unresolved member used to be bound to whatever variable or method happened to be named name, which is not Java's meaning (ADR-060).
diagnostics.fix: Give the receiver its record or ledger type instead of var or PlutusData, or call a static helper as helper(x) rather than x.helper().

diagnostics.title: Loop assignment to a shared static field or @Param
diagnostics.template: Assignment to field ''{0}'' in a loop is not supported: {1}
diagnostics.summary: Static fields and @Param fields are not shared state on-chain: a loop assignment rebinds the name only in the rest of the assigning method's current run, and every other run and every other method sees the initial value. The assignment is accepted only where that matches Java: the field is not final, the method is an entry method (a validator entrypoint or the compileMethod target) that no method calls, the loop is not in a lambda, and no other method reads the field (ADR-060).
diagnostics.fix: Copy the field into a local accumulator before the loop, update the local, and pass it to the methods that need it.

diagnostics.title: Static field initializer calls a method of its class
diagnostics.template: Static field ''{0}'' calls method {1}; static field initializers cannot call methods of their class
diagnostics.summary: Static field initializers are evaluated outside the class's methods, so a call to one of them cannot be bound.
diagnostics.fix: Call the method where the value is used, or initialise the field with an expression that does not call a method of this class.

diagnostics.title: Reassignment in a loop that updates no earlier variable
diagnostics.template: Reassigning {0} ''{1}'' is not supported in a loop that updates no variable declared before the loop
diagnostics.summary: A for-each loop can reassign its loop variable or a local declared in its body only while it also updates a variable declared before the loop. Without one, the body is compiled as plain statements, which cannot reassign a variable (ADR-060).
diagnostics.fix: Declare a new local for the new value instead of reassigning, for example var adjusted = amount.subtract(fee);

diagnostics.title: instanceof pattern variable reuses a field name
diagnostics.template: Pattern variable ''{0}'' has the same name as a field of {1}
diagnostics.summary: An instanceof pattern variable is bound only when the pattern is the whole condition of an if statement outside a loop. In any other position (a loop body, an && condition, a negated guard, a ternary, a lambda) the name resolves to a field of the same name instead, which silently reads or updates the field (#204). A pattern variable may therefore not reuse the name of a field, including a @Param field, of an enclosing class.
diagnostics.fix: Rename the pattern variable, for example `if (action instanceof Bid bid)`, so it does not reuse a field name.

diagnostics.title: continue is not supported
diagnostics.template: continue is not supported on-chain
diagnostics.summary: `continue` is outside the on-chain subset. Loops are compiled to folds and recursive functions whose body runs to its end on every iteration; there is no lowering that skips the rest of the body. The diagnostic is reported when the compiler lowers the loop that contains the `continue`, so code JuLC does not compile, such as a nested off-chain helper class, is not affected.
diagnostics.fix: Guard the rest of the loop body with an if instead: replace `if (skip) { continue; } rest;` with `if (!skip) { rest; }`.

diagnostics.title: Reassignment outside a loop
diagnostics.template: Reassigning ''{0}'' is not supported outside a loop
diagnostics.summary: On-chain variables are single-assignment. Only a loop can update a variable declared before it (the loop's accumulator); anywhere else, assigning to a local variable, parameter or field is rejected, including in an if/else branch and inside an expression.
diagnostics.fix: Declare a new local for the new value, for example `long squared = x * n;`, or choose the value in one expression, for example `var limit = vip ? BigInteger.valueOf(100) : BigInteger.TEN;`.

diagnostics.title: JulcMap.of is off-chain only
diagnostics.template: JulcMap.of is off-chain only and has no on-chain implementation
diagnostics.summary: `JulcMap.of(...)` builds a `JulcAssocMap` in Java, for tests and off-chain code. The compiler has no lowering for it. On-chain, a map is built from `JulcMap.empty()` with `insert`, which adds the entry at the front of the map.
diagnostics.fix: Build the map from JulcMap.empty() with insert, for example `JulcMap<byte[], BigInteger> map = JulcMap.<byte[], BigInteger>empty().insert(key, value);`. insert adds at the front, so JulcMap.of(a, x, b, y) is `JulcMap.<K, V>empty().insert(b, y).insert(a, x)`.

example.bad: JulcMap<byte[], BigInteger> map = JulcMap.of(key, BigInteger.ONE);
example.good: JulcMap<byte[], BigInteger> map = JulcMap.<byte[], BigInteger>empty().insert(key, BigInteger.ONE);

diagnostics.title: break in a loop that updates no earlier variable
diagnostics.template: break is not supported in a loop that updates no variable declared before the loop
diagnostics.summary: A loop supports `break` only when it updates a variable declared before the loop. A loop that updates none compiles its body as plain statements, which cannot stop the loop. This holds also when the loop is nested inside another loop (T26, #273). A loop whose only update is in a position the compiler cannot carry, such as a switch statement or an expression, reports JULC0065 at the update instead.
diagnostics.fix: Declare a variable before the loop and set it where the loop breaks: `boolean stopped = false;` before the loop and `if (found) { stopped = true; break; }` in it.

diagnostics.title: Unsupported statement in a loop with break
diagnostics.template: {0} is not supported in a loop that contains break and updates one variable declared before the loop
diagnostics.summary: A loop that contains `break` and updates exactly one variable declared before it may contain only variable declarations, assignments, if/else and break. A nested while or for-each loop in its body is rejected with this code; another unsupported statement keeps its own diagnostic. A loop that updates two or more such variables supports nested loops.
diagnostics.fix: Move the nested loop into a helper method that returns the value it computes, and call the helper from the loop body.

diagnostics.title: Loop update in a position the loop cannot carry
diagnostics.template: Updating ''{0}'' {1} is not supported in this loop
diagnostics.summary: A loop carries an update of a variable declared before it only when the update is a statement of its own, directly in the loop body or in an if/else branch. An update in the loop condition or iterable, inside a switch statement, inside an expression or inside a lambda is not seen as one, so a loop with break whose only updates are there reports this code at the update. The code is emitted only for such a loop with break; the same update in a loop without break still has an uncoded diagnostic (#206).
diagnostics.fix: Write the update as a statement of its own, directly in the loop body or in an if/else branch: for example `if (k == 1) { c = c + 1; } else { c = c + 2; }` instead of a switch statement, `c = c + 1;` before the `if` instead of `if ((c = c + 1) > 5)`, and `while (x - 1 > 0) { x = x - 1; ... }` instead of `while ((x = x - 1) > 0)`.

diagnostics.title: Labels are not supported
diagnostics.template: Labels are not supported on-chain: ''{0}''
diagnostics.summary: Labelled statements are outside the on-chain subset, so no `break` or `continue` can name a label. A `break` that named a label used to be accepted and compiled as a plain `break` of the innermost loop, even when no statement carried the label (#201); javac rejects that source, but tools that compile source text without javac did not. A labelled statement, a `break` that names a label and a `continue` that names a label all report this code, located at the labelled statement, the `break` or the `continue`, whether or not a matching label exists. The diagnostic is reported when the compiler lowers the code, so code JuLC does not compile, such as a nested off-chain helper class, is not affected; only a labelled `break` outside any loop, which subset validation already rejected, is reported there.
diagnostics.fix: Remove the label. To leave an outer loop from an inner one, declare a variable before the loops, set it where the inner loop breaks and skip the rest of the outer loop while it is set: `boolean stop = false; for (var x : xs) { if (!stop) { for (var y : ys) { if (found) { stop = true; break; } } } }`. continue is not supported with or without a label (JULC0060).

diagnostics.title: Integer literal javac rejects
diagnostics.template: Integer literal {0} is invalid: {1}
diagnostics.summary: An int literal has 32 bits and a long literal 64 (JLS 21 §3.10.1). A decimal literal must fit the signed range; 2147483648 and 9223372036854775808L are allowed only directly after a unary minus, not inside parentheses. A hexadecimal, octal or binary literal must fit the width, and denotes the two's-complement value of its bits, so 0xFFFFFFFF is -1. An octal literal has only the digits 0 to 7. A byte[] initializer element must be in -128 to 127. javac rejects any other literal, and so does JuLC.
diagnostics.fix: Add the L suffix for a long literal, use BigInteger for a larger value, write a negated most-negative literal without parentheses (-2147483648), and keep byte[] elements in -128 to 127.

example.bad:
long big = 4294967296;
byte[] b = new byte[]{0xFF};
example.good:
long big = 4294967296L;
byte[] b = new byte[]{-1};

diagnostics.title: Switch label is dominated by an earlier label
diagnostics.template: Switch label ''{0}'' is dominated by {1} and can never be selected
diagnostics.summary: A case label is dominated when a preceding unguarded label already matches every value it matches, or when a `default` label precedes a pattern label (JLS 14.11.1, 14.30.3). javac rejects such a switch; JuLC used to compile it with first-match meaning (ADR-067 D4).
diagnostics.fix: Remove the dominated label, or move the more specific (or guarded) label before the general one and `default` last.

diagnostics.title: Switch guard is not a usable boolean condition
diagnostics.template: Invalid guard on ''{0}'': {1}
diagnostics.summary: A guard (`when`) must have type boolean or Boolean, and must not be a constant expression with value false, such as `false`, a `static final boolean` that is false, or `1 == 2` (JLS 14.11.1). A constant `true` guard is allowed and makes the label unguarded (ADR-067 D1, D4).
diagnostics.fix: Use a boolean condition that depends on the matched value or other inputs; delete an arm whose guard is always false.

example.bad: case A a when 3 -> ONE;
example.good: case A a when a.v().compareTo(BigInteger.valueOf(3)) > 0 -> ONE;

diagnostics.title: Switch guard reads a variable that is reassigned
diagnostics.template: Guard on ''{0}'' reads ''{1}'', which is reassigned; a variable used in a guard must be final or effectively final
diagnostics.summary: Any local variable or parameter used but not declared in a guard must be final or effectively final (JLS 14.11.1, 4.12.4). In JuLC only loops reassign variables, so this is a variable a loop updates. The check uses the declaration the name resolves to, not the name (ADR-067 D4).
diagnostics.fix: Copy the variable's final value into a new local after the loop, and use that local in the guard.

diagnostics.title: Switch guard introduces a pattern variable
diagnostics.template: Guard on ''{0}'' declares pattern variable ''{1}'', which is not supported
diagnostics.summary: Java lets a guard introduce pattern variables (`when p.t() instanceof C c`, JLS 6.3.3), but JuLC binds instanceof pattern variables only as the whole condition of an if statement (#204). A guard may still use instanceof as a plain type test (ADR-067 D1).
diagnostics.fix: Use a nested record pattern instead, `case P(C c) -> c.w()`, or test the type without a binding (`p.t() instanceof C`) and read the value in the arm.

example.bad: case P p when p.t() instanceof C c -> c.w();
example.good: case P p when p.t() instanceof C -> ((C) p.t()).w();

diagnostics.title: Colon-form switch group is not supported
diagnostics.template: Unsupported switch group ''{0}'': {1}
diagnostics.summary: JuLC compiles a colon-form switch expression only when every statement group has exactly one label and yields on every path. Java lets a group fall through into the next one; JuLC does not implement fall-through, and used to return the group's last expression instead (#283). Several labels on one group, or several patterns in one label, are rejected too (ADR-067 D4, I16).
diagnostics.fix: End every group with `yield`, give each group its own label, or use the arrow form `case X x -> ...`.

example.bad:
case A x: x.v().negate();
default: yield BigInteger.TWO;
example.good:
case A x: yield x.v().negate();
default: yield BigInteger.TWO;

diagnostics.title: Case pattern is not supported
diagnostics.template: Unsupported case pattern ''{0}'': {1}
diagnostics.summary: A case pattern must name a permitted variant of the selector's sealed interface. A pattern for a type that is not a variant is not applicable; the total type pattern `case S s` on a selector of type S is valid Java but not supported (ADR-067 D3, D4).
diagnostics.fix: Name a permitted variant in each case label, and use `default` for the remaining ones.

example.bad: case S t -> 2;
example.good: default -> 2;

diagnostics.title: instanceof with a pattern JuLC does not lower
diagnostics.template: Unsupported instanceof pattern: {0}
diagnostics.summary: An instanceof whose pattern is not a type pattern, such as a record pattern (ADR-067 D3), is not supported. Emitted by the javac frontend (ADR-068 I2a); the reference frontend reports it uncoded.
diagnostics.fix: Use a type pattern (x instanceof R r) and read the components through r, or a switch.

diagnostics.title: equals between types that can never be equal
diagnostics.template: {0} compares {1} with {2}, which Java keeps distinct: on-chain the two can compare equal
diagnostics.summary: An equals call or collection operation whose JVM implementation compares with equals, between static types that are not related: neither is a subtype of the other by class, or a type argument is not related to the same argument of the other (ADR-067 D5, ADR-068 D6). Java's answer is false, and on-chain a comparison reads representations, so an integer and a long, a string and its bytes, or two records with the same fields can be equal. Emitted by the javac frontend.
diagnostics.fix: Compare through one typed value (decode the datum to the record type first), or compare the components explicitly.

diagnostics.title: Record implements two sealed interfaces
diagnostics.template: Record {0} implements sealed interfaces {1} and {2}; a record may have at most one sealed parent
diagnostics.summary: A Data value has one constructor tag, so a record cannot be a variant of two sealed interfaces (ADR-067 D6). Emitted by the javac frontend (ADR-068 D11).
diagnostics.fix: Wrap the record in a separate variant for the second interface.

diagnostics.title: Record body member is not supported
diagnostics.template: Record {0} declares {1}, which JuLC does not compile; a record body may contain only nested type declarations
diagnostics.summary: JuLC compiles a record as its components only, so a declared accessor, equals, constructor, method, static field or initializer would be ignored (ADR-067 D9). Emitted by the javac frontend (ADR-068 D11).
diagnostics.fix: Move the logic into a static helper method of the enclosing class.

diagnostics.title: Source redeclares or extends a JuLC API type or bundled library
diagnostics.template: {0} declares {1}, which JuLC''s {2} owns
diagnostics.summary: JuLC's on-chain API (julc-core, julc-ledger-api, the stdlib's on-chain classes, julc-verification's annotations) and its bundled stdlib libraries come only from JuLC. A source is a bundled library only if its text is the shipped one (by digest); any other source that declares a type with an API or bundled name, or in a package they define, is rejected before javac runs, so no source can replace or extend them (ADR-068 D3, generalizing ADR-067 D9's ledger redeclaration). The javac gate emits it in enforce mode, the default (ADR-068 M1); ADR-067's simple-name rule for ledger hash types is still planned.
diagnostics.fix: Rename the type, or move it to a package of your own.

example.bad:
package org.julclang.ledger;

record Value(java.math.BigInteger lovelace) {}
example.good:
package com.example;

record Amount(java.math.BigInteger lovelace) {}

diagnostics.title: Switch has more than one default label
diagnostics.template: Switch has more than one default label (second at {0})
diagnostics.summary: A switch block may have at most one default label (JLS 14.11.1). JuLC used to let the second replace the first (ADR-067 D4).
diagnostics.fix: Keep one `default` label.

example.good:
case A a -> 1;
default -> 2;

diagnostics.title: Pattern variable redeclares a variable in scope
diagnostics.template: Pattern variable ''{0}'' is already defined {1}
diagnostics.summary: A pattern variable may not have the name of a local variable, parameter or pattern variable in scope, and a pattern may not declare one name twice (JLS 6.4, 14.30.1). JuLC used to let it shadow the outer variable. It may have the name of a field, as in Java (ADR-067 D4).
diagnostics.fix: Rename the pattern variable.

diagnostics.title: Construct not yet ported to the javac frontend
diagnostics.template: The javac frontend does not compile {0} yet
diagnostics.summary: Retired at ADR-068 M6, never reused: the javac frontend had not ported a construct. No compilation reports it: every construct of the subset is lowered or has a code of its own.
diagnostics.fix: None: no compilation reports this code.

diagnostics.title: javac rejects the source
diagnostics.summary: Source that is not valid Java is rejected with javac's own diagnostic: its message, its key (such as compiler.err.cant.resolve.location) and its position, with the column counted in characters from the line start. JuLC's closed environment (ADR-068 I10) adds a hint where a name is missing because JuLC does not provide it: a JDK type or package outside JuLC's platform, or an annotation from outside the on-chain API. Emitted by the javac frontend, the default from ADR-068 M5, and by the javac gate in enforce mode ahead of the JavaParser frontend (ADR-068 D5, M1).
diagnostics.fix: Fix the Java error javac reports; where the hint names a JDK type, use JuLC's on-chain equivalent.

example.bad: BigInteger total = a + b;
example.good: BigInteger total = a.add(b);

diagnostics.title: Reference equality is not supported
diagnostics.template: {0} compares {1} by reference; use equals
diagnostics.summary: == and != on BigInteger, byte[], String, boxed values or records is reference equality in Java (JLS 15.21.3), but value equality on-chain (ADR-068 D6). Constant String operands built from literals and string + alone keep their meaning, and any other constant comparison stops too, in a guard unless the guard is constant as a whole. Emitted by the javac frontend.
diagnostics.fix: Use a.equals(b), or Builtins.equalsByteString(a, b) for bytes (ByteStringLib.equals(a, b) is equivalent).

diagnostics.title: Equality would compare an array by identity
diagnostics.template: {0} compares {1}, whose equality on the JVM {2}
diagnostics.summary: An equals call or collection operation whose JVM implementation compares elements or keys with equals, at a static type through which an array is compared by identity (directly, or through record components, sealed variants or type arguments), is true on-chain for equal bytes but false on the JVM (ADR-068 D6). A type the check cannot read (a raw collection, Object, a type variable, an operand of no readable type) is rejected the same way, because it cannot be shown to compare by value. Emitted by the javac frontend.
diagnostics.fix: Compare the bytes: Builtins.equalsByteString(a, b) for byte[] (ByteStringLib.equals(a, b) is equivalent, a few bytes larger), and Builtins.equalsByteString(a.value(), b.value()) on the component accessors of a @NewType byte wrapper. Where the type cannot be read, compare at the value's own declared type.

diagnostics.title: @Param field is a Java constant variable
diagnostics.template: @Param field {0} is a constant variable in Java, so javac would fold it; it is runtime input
diagnostics.summary: A static final primitive or String @Param field with a constant initializer is a constant variable to javac, which folds it, so the JVM program would not be the script that receives the applied parameter (ADR-068 D14).
diagnostics.fix: Drop final, or initialize from a non-constant expression such as Boolean.valueOf(true).

diagnostics.title: The host's javac is missing or not supported
diagnostics.template: javac on Java {0} is not supported: {1}
diagnostics.summary: JuLC reads Java with the host's javac (ToolProvider.getSystemJavaCompiler), against a platform built for javac feature release 25. A runtime without the jdk.compiler module, or a javac whose highest source version is not RELEASE_25, is rejected (ADR-068 D3, I6). Emitted by the javac frontend, the default from ADR-068 M5, and by the javac gate in enforce mode ahead of the JavaParser frontend (ADR-068 M1).
diagnostics.fix: Run JuLC on a JDK 25 runtime that includes jdk.compiler.

diagnostics.title: String concatenation with a non-String operand
diagnostics.template: String concatenation {0} has a non-String operand of type {1}
diagnostics.summary: "a" + 1 is valid Java, but JuLC lowers string + to appendString, which fails at run time on an integer (ADR-068 D6, #296). A switch guard that is a constant expression as a whole keeps its meaning. Emitted by the javac frontend.
diagnostics.fix: Concatenate Strings only.

diagnostics.title: Native array in a Data-encoded position
diagnostics.template: {0} needs a Data encoding of the native array {1}, which has none
diagnostics.summary: A JulcArray is a native UPLC array, which has no Data encoding (ADR-068 D6, #298). A record or sealed-variant component, a type argument of Optional, Tuple2, Tuple3, JulcList, JulcMap or JulcArray, and a @Param or compileMethod input are Data-encoded, so an array there compiled but failed on-chain where the Java code succeeds. An array of Data-encodable elements, such as JulcArray<JulcList<BigInteger>>, is supported.
diagnostics.fix: Store a JulcList in the record, collection or input, and build the array where it is used, for example `xs.toArray()` in a local.

diagnostics.title: Sealed interface needs a permits clause
diagnostics.template: Sealed interface ''{0}'' has no permits clause, and its permitted subclasses ({1}) are not exactly the records nested in it
diagnostics.summary: A variant's Data tag is its position in the permits clause; without one, among the records nested in the interface, in member order. Java also permits other classes of the compilation unit implicitly, such as a top-level or sibling-nested record, and those have no tag under that rule (ADR-068 I11). The javac frontend rejects the interface rather than choose an order.
diagnostics.fix: Add a permits clause listing every variant, in tag order.

example.bad:
sealed interface Shape {}
record Circle(BigInteger r) implements Shape {}
example.good:
sealed interface Shape permits Circle {}
record Circle(BigInteger r) implements Shape {}

diagnostics.title: String literal holds an unpaired surrogate
diagnostics.template: A string literal holds the unpaired surrogate U+{0}, which a UPLC string cannot hold
diagnostics.summary: javac accepts a lone surrogate in a string literal, but a UPLC string is Unicode text: the script's FLAT encoding would carry a ? in its place, so the JVM program would not be the script (ADR-065, ADR-068 I2a).
diagnostics.fix: Write a supplementary character as its high surrogate followed by its low surrogate, or remove it.

diagnostics.title: An entry point returns boolean
diagnostics.template: Entrypoint {0} of {1} returns {2}; an entry point returns boolean or java.lang.Boolean
diagnostics.summary: An @Entrypoint method of a validator states its verdict as a boolean or Boolean. Any other return type is not a validator's result.
diagnostics.fix: Declare the method to return boolean.

example.bad:
@Entrypoint
public static BigInteger validate(PlutusData redeemer, ScriptContext ctx) { return BigInteger.ONE; }
example.good:
@Entrypoint
public static boolean validate(PlutusData redeemer, ScriptContext ctx) { return true; }

diagnostics.title: An initializer that is not lowered holds only a constant
diagnostics.template: {0} is not lowered, so {1}
diagnostics.summary: A static field of the compiled class is lowered. Any other field initializer (a @Param field, an instance field, a field of another type, a field of a library, whose static fields bind at script start) and any initializer block is not, so it holds only a literal, a new byte[]{...} of literals, BigInteger.ZERO, ONE, TWO or TEN, PlutusData.UNIT, or a constant variable. Boolean.valueOf(true) and Boolean.valueOf(false) are allowed for a @Param field that must not be a constant variable. An initializer block is empty.
diagnostics.fix: Move the value to a static field of the compiled class, or to the entry point, or write it as a literal.

example.bad: class Limits { static BigInteger MAX = BigInteger.valueOf(5); }
example.good:
@SpendingValidator
class V { static final BigInteger MAX = BigInteger.valueOf(5); }

diagnostics.title: A + of string constants is joined when the script runs
diagnostics.template: These string constants are joined when the script runs: Java joins them when it compiles, and JuLC keeps the + as written
diagnostics.summary: Java joins string constants when it compiles. JuLC keeps a + as written, so the script joins them each time it runs. A constant is a string literal, a String variable that javac gives a constant value, or a + of constants, through parentheses. One warning covers a whole expression of constants. The warning comes from the rule that reads javac's trees, so it needs the javac gate on the JavaParser frontend, and it rejects nothing.
diagnostics.fix: Write one string literal.

example.bad: static String greeting() { return "hello " + "world"; }
example.good: static String greeting() { return "hello world"; }

diagnostics.title: A record does not declare a method its Data would skip
diagnostics.template: {0} has a name JuLC reads in place of its body, so a program does not declare it
diagnostics.summary: JuLC compiles a record as its components, so a declared toPlutusData or an explicit accessor is never what a script's Data is, and a generated accessor that implements ToPlutusData.toPlutusData is not lowered.
diagnostics.fix: Give the method or component another name, and read the component through its generated accessor.

example.bad: record Amount(BigInteger v) { public BigInteger v() { return v.abs(); } }
example.good: record Amount(BigInteger v) { static BigInteger size(Amount a) { return a.v().abs(); } }

diagnostics.title: A name JuLC reads by its spelling binds to what JuLC reads
diagnostics.template: JuLC reads {0} as {1}, and here it is {2}, so a program does not write it
diagnostics.summary: Retired at ADR-068 M6, never reused: a name the JavaParser frontend read by its spelling bound elsewhere. javac binds every name to its declaration, so no compilation reports it.
diagnostics.fix: None: no compilation reports this code.

example.bad: @NewType record Boolean(BigInteger v) { }
example.good: @NewType record Flag(BigInteger v) { }

diagnostics.title: A constructor holds no statement
diagnostics.template: The body of constructor {0} does not run on-chain, so a constructor holds no statement
diagnostics.summary: A value is built from its components alone, so a constructor's body never runs on-chain. Any constructor a source declares, on a record or a class, holds no statement.
diagnostics.fix: Move the statement to a method, and call the method where the value is made.

example.bad: record Amount(BigInteger v) { Amount { v = v.abs(); } }
example.good: record Amount(BigInteger v) { static Amount of(BigInteger v) { return new Amount(v.abs()); } }

diagnostics.title: A value reaches boolean through a cast only from a boolean
diagnostics.template: A cast to {0} takes a boolean or a Boolean, not {1}
diagnostics.summary: A cast to boolean or Boolean, or a call JuLC lowers to its argument with that result, such as PlutusData.cast, takes an operand whose type, through parentheses and other casts, is boolean or Boolean.
diagnostics.fix: Compare the value to get a boolean.

example.bad: boolean b = (boolean)(Object) amount;
example.good: boolean b = amount.signum() > 0;

diagnostics.title: A program has one validator class, and a single-purpose validator one entry point
diagnostics.template: {0} declares more than one {1}
diagnostics.summary: A compilation unit holds one validator class, and a single-purpose validator one @Entrypoint method. Only a @MultiValidator has several, one per purpose.
diagnostics.fix: Keep one, or use @MultiValidator with a purpose on each @Entrypoint.

diagnostics.title: An entry point is static
diagnostics.template: Entrypoint {0} of {1} is not static
diagnostics.summary: An @Entrypoint method is static.
diagnostics.fix: Declare the method static.

diagnostics.title: An entry point's last parameter is the script context
diagnostics.template: Entrypoint {0} of {1} takes {2} as its last parameter; the last parameter is the script context, ScriptContext or PlutusData
diagnostics.summary: The wrapper passes the script context's Data as an entry point's last argument, undecoded. A last parameter of another type reads the context as that type, so the script does not do what the JVM test of the method does (ADR-068 F904).
diagnostics.fix: Declare the last parameter as ScriptContext, or as PlutusData to keep the context as Data. Read other values from the redeemer or the datum.

example.bad:
@Entrypoint
static boolean validate(BigInteger redeemer, BigInteger ctx) { return true; }
example.good:
@Entrypoint
static boolean validate(BigInteger redeemer, ScriptContext ctx) { return true; }

diagnostics.title: synchronized is not supported
diagnostics.template: synchronized is not supported on-chain
diagnostics.summary: A synchronized block has no on-chain meaning. Emitted by the javac frontend (ADR-068 I2a); the reference frontend reports it uncoded.
diagnostics.fix: On-chain code is single-threaded; remove synchronized blocks

diagnostics.title: Method references are not supported
diagnostics.template: Method references (::) are not supported on-chain
diagnostics.summary: A method reference has no on-chain lowering. Emitted by the javac frontend (ADR-068 I2a); the reference frontend reports it uncoded.
diagnostics.fix: Use a regular static method call instead

diagnostics.title: A call through a functional interface is not supported
diagnostics.template: Functional interface .{0}() is not supported on-chain
diagnostics.summary: A function exists on-chain only as the argument of the list method that applies it, so a local of a functional interface type cannot be called. Emitted by the javac frontend (ADR-068 I2a); the reference frontend reports it uncoded.
diagnostics.fix: Call the method directly instead of through a function reference

diagnostics.title: 'this' and 'super' are not supported
diagnostics.template: ''{0}'' is not supported on-chain
diagnostics.summary: On-chain code has no objects and no inheritance, so this and super name nothing. Emitted by the javac frontend (ADR-068 I2a); the reference frontend reports it uncoded.
diagnostics.fix: On-chain validators are stateless; use static methods, and sealed interfaces with record variants instead of inheritance

diagnostics.title: Array access is not supported
diagnostics.template: array access is not supported on-chain
diagnostics.summary: An array element read or write has no on-chain lowering. Emitted by the javac frontend (ADR-068 I2a); the reference frontend reports it uncoded.
diagnostics.fix: Use List<T> with list operations instead

diagnostics.title: Class inheritance is not supported
diagnostics.template: class inheritance is not supported on-chain
diagnostics.summary: A class that extends another class, or an interface that extends another, has no on-chain meaning. Emitted by the javac frontend (ADR-068 I2a); the reference frontend reports it uncoded.
diagnostics.fix: Use sealed interfaces with record variants instead

diagnostics.title: Statement is not supported
diagnostics.template: Unsupported statement: {0}
diagnostics.summary: A bare block, an empty statement or a switch statement among a method's statements has no lowering. Emitted by the javac frontend (ADR-068 I2a); the reference frontend reports it uncoded.
diagnostics.fix: Only variable declarations, if/else, for-each, while, return, and expression statements are supported on-chain.

diagnostics.title: return inside a for-each loop
diagnostics.template: 'return' is not supported inside for-each loop body
diagnostics.summary: A for-each loop is compiled to a fold whose result is the variables the loop updates, so its body cannot return from the method. Emitted by the javac frontend (ADR-068 I2a); the reference frontend reports it uncoded.
diagnostics.fix: Use 'break' to exit the loop early, then return after the loop. Or use the accumulator pattern: result = value; (continue iterating) then return result; after the loop.

diagnostics.title: yield inside a loop
diagnostics.template: ''yield'' is not supported inside {0} loop body
diagnostics.summary: A loop body cannot yield a value of an enclosing switch expression. Emitted by the javac frontend (ADR-068 I2a); the reference frontend reports it uncoded.
diagnostics.fix: Use 'break' to exit the loop early, then yield after the loop. Or use the accumulator pattern: result = value; (continue iterating) then yield result; after the loop.

diagnostics.title: A loop-body local is updated in a branch
diagnostics.template: Conditional update to loop-body local ''{0}'' is not supported
diagnostics.summary: An if/else branch in a loop carries only the loop's accumulators out of the branch, so an update of a local declared in the loop body would be lost. Emitted by the javac frontend (ADR-068 I2a); the reference frontend reports it uncoded.
diagnostics.fix: An if/else branch carries only loop accumulators out of the branch. Use a conditional initializer (condition ? value : otherValue), or declare the variable before the loop so it is an accumulator (reset it each iteration if needed), or declare it inside the branch if its value is only needed there.

diagnostics.title: Assignment at a position with no lowering
diagnostics.template: Assignment to {0} is not supported at this position
diagnostics.summary: Inside a loop, an assignment is lowered only as a statement directly in the loop body or in an if/else branch of it. Emitted by the javac frontend (ADR-068 I2a); the reference frontend reports it uncoded.
diagnostics.fix: Inside a loop, assign an accumulator or a loop-body local as a statement directly in the loop body. In an if/else branch, assign an accumulator or a local declared within that branch; an assignment inside another expression or statement is not supported.

diagnostics.title: Statement is not supported in this loop body
diagnostics.template: Unsupported {0} body: {1}
diagnostics.summary: A loop that breaks, or that updates several variables declared before it, lowers only declarations, assignments, if/else and break in its body. Emitted by the javac frontend (ADR-068 I2a); the reference frontend reports it uncoded.
diagnostics.fix: Inside loops with break or several accumulators, only variable declarations, assignments, if/else, and break are supported.

diagnostics.title: Assignment to a variable with no binder
diagnostics.template: Assignment to undeclared variable ''{0}''
diagnostics.summary: A loop assigns a name that is neither an accumulator of the loop nor a local of its body, such as a field. Emitted by the javac frontend (ADR-068 I2a); the reference frontend reports it uncoded.
diagnostics.fix: Declare the variable before assigning it: before the loop for an accumulator, in the loop body for a local.

diagnostics.title: Compound assignment on a type it has no lowering for
diagnostics.template: Compound assignment {0} to ''{1}'' {2}
diagnostics.summary: Compound assignment is lowered on integer variables, and += on String variables with a String operand. Emitted by the javac frontend (ADR-068 I2a); the reference frontend reports it uncoded.
diagnostics.fix: Write the update explicitly, e.g. x = x.add(y), or convert the right-hand side to the variable's type first.

diagnostics.title: Operator is not supported
diagnostics.template: Unsupported operator: {0}
diagnostics.summary: A binary operator with no on-chain lowering, such as a shift or a bitwise operator. Emitted by the javac frontend (ADR-068 I2a); the reference frontend reports it uncoded.

diagnostics.title: Unary operator is not supported
diagnostics.template: Unsupported unary operator: {0}
diagnostics.summary: A unary operator with no on-chain lowering, such as ~, + or an increment outside a loop update. Emitted by the javac frontend (ADR-068 I2a); the reference frontend reports it uncoded.
diagnostics.fix: Supported unary operators: ! (logical NOT) and - (negation)

diagnostics.title: A switch pattern variable is reassigned
diagnostics.template: Reassignment of switch case-pattern variable ''{0}'' is not supported
diagnostics.summary: An arm of a switch reads a pattern variable through projections of the matched record, so an assignment to it would not be seen. Emitted by the javac frontend (ADR-068 I2a); the reference frontend reports it uncoded.
diagnostics.fix: Copy the pattern variable to a fresh local accumulator inside the arm, update that local, and yield its result instead.

diagnostics.title: A switch expression arm updates an enclosing variable
diagnostics.template: Switch-expression arm cannot update enclosing variable ''{0}''
diagnostics.summary: A switch expression exports only its yielded value, so an update of a variable declared outside the arm would be lost. Emitted by the javac frontend (ADR-068 I2a); the reference frontend reports it uncoded.
diagnostics.fix: A switch expression exports only its yielded value. Declare an accumulator inside the arm, yield its result, and use the switch value outside the arm instead of mutating an enclosing variable.

diagnostics.title: A generic library method is called from Java
diagnostics.template: Generic library method {0} cannot be called from Java yet: generic @OnchainLibrary methods are specialized only by language-neutral library providers (ADR-059). Provide a concrete overload-free method for Java callers.
diagnostics.summary: A generic @OnchainLibrary method is a template that only a language-neutral producer instantiates (ADR-059), so Java code cannot call it. Emitted by the javac frontend (ADR-068 I2a); the reference frontend reports it uncoded.
diagnostics.fix: Provide a concrete overload-free method for Java callers.

diagnostics.title: A static call names its class by a qualified name
diagnostics.template: Static call {0} names its class by a qualified name; on-chain code calls a static method through its class''s simple name
diagnostics.summary: JuLC resolves a static call through the simple name of its class, as an import or the enclosing class declares it. A call through a package-qualified class name, such as java.math.BigInteger.valueOf(1), is not resolved. Emitted by the javac frontend (ADR-068 I2a); the reference frontend reports it uncoded, as an undefined name, or as JULC0062 for JulcMap.of. A nested class's qualified name, Outer.Inner.f(a), is the reference's JULC0011.
diagnostics.fix: Import the class and call the method through its simple name, for example `import java.math.BigInteger;` and `BigInteger.valueOf(1)`.

diagnostics.title: A primitive type with no on-chain representation
diagnostics.template: Unsupported primitive type: {0}. Supported types: boolean, int, long
diagnostics.summary: byte, short, char, float and double have no on-chain representation, as a variable's, a component's or a cast's type. Emitted by the javac frontend (ADR-068 I2a), in the reference frontend's words, which it reports uncoded. A char literal elsewhere is JULC0125, in the reference's words for it.
diagnostics.fix: Use int or long for a number, BigInteger for an unbounded integer, boolean for a flag, and String or byte[] for text and bytes.

diagnostics.title: An expression outside the subset
diagnostics.template: Unsupported expression: {0}
diagnostics.summary: An expression form JuLC does not compile on-chain: a class literal, a text block, a function that is not a lambda written at the call, and the like. Emitted by the javac frontend (ADR-068 I2a); the reference frontend reports the same family uncoded, in these words, or as an undefined name.
diagnostics.fix: Write the value with a supported form: a string literal for a text block, a lambda at the call for a function, and no class literal outside PlutusData.cast.

diagnostics.title: instanceof of a value whose type is not the variant's sealed interface
diagnostics.template: {0} tests a value of type {1}, which is not {2} or a variant of it; on-chain the test reads a constructor tag, which another type can share
diagnostics.summary: An instanceof pattern on a variant reads the value's constructor tag. That answers Java's question only when the value's static type is the variant's sealed interface or the variant itself: a value of another type, through a widening cast to Object for one, can carry the same tag. Emitted by the javac frontend (ADR-068 M5); the reference frontend reads the tag.
diagnostics.fix: Test a value of the sealed interface's type, or switch over it.

diagnostics.title: A variant that is not a plain record
diagnostics.template: {0} is a variant of {1} that is not a plain record; a variant is a record, not a class or a @NewType, so that it has one constructor tag and its fields
diagnostics.summary: JuLC encodes a sealed interface's value as a constructor whose tag is the variant's place among the permitted records, and whose fields are the record's components. A final class or a @NewType has neither. Emitted by the javac frontend at a new, an instanceof or a case of such a variant, and otherwise at the variant's declaration wherever its sealed interface is declared in a unit the compilation reads, whether or not the program reads the sum: such a sum has no layout (ADR-068 M5). The reference frontend reads it as a record of no or one field.
diagnostics.fix: Make the variant a record that is not a @NewType.

diagnostics.title: A value whose on-chain form is not the one the operation reads
diagnostics.summary: The value's on-chain representation is not the one this operation takes, and no conversion keeps Java's value: Data where a builtin takes bytes, a native list where a component holds Data, a ledger type that holds a map, whose Data repeats a key the JVM's map holds once. Emitted by the javac frontend (ADR-068 M5) where the reference reads the representation as it finds it and fails or misreads.
diagnostics.fix: Convert explicitly: Builtins.unBData for bytes, Builtins.listData or mapData for a list or a map, or read the map through the stdlib's ValuesLib and MapLib.

diagnostics.title: A class instance is constructed
diagnostics.template: Cannot construct non-record type: {0}
diagnostics.summary: A new of a class that is not a record, a tuple, a sealed variant or a supported API type. On-chain a value is a record's components, and a class's constructor and fields have no on-chain form. Emitted by the javac frontend (ADR-068 I2a); the reference frontend reports it uncoded.
diagnostics.fix: Only record types can be constructed on-chain. Declare the type as a record.

diagnostics.title: A compound assignment narrows a long to int
diagnostics.template: Compound assignment {0} to the int ''{1}'' takes a long: Java narrows the result to 32 bits and the on-chain integer does not, so a JVM test and the script could differ
diagnostics.summary: An int variable updated with +=, -=, *=, /= or %= from a long operand. Java casts the result back to int without saying so, and an on-chain integer has no width, so past 32 bits the JVM and the script would give different values. Emitted by the javac frontend (ADR-068 r19).
diagnostics.fix: Declare the variable as long, e.g. long total = 0; total += amount; (BigInteger for values that can pass 64 bits). If you do want Java's 32-bit result, write the cast: x = (int) (x + y);
